name: Four Seasons Hotel Casa Medina Bogota
positioning: Four Seasons hotel in a landmark 1946 building in Bogota's Zona G, with 62 accommodations
best_for: Travelers who want a Four Seasons stay in a restored 1946 building
Travelers who want to be in Zona G, the city's gastronomy district

facts.text: The hotel is in a landmark 1946 building designed by Colombian artist-architect Santiago Medina Mejia.
The hotel is in the heart of the city's Zona G, the gastronomy district.
Castanyoles is a stylish Spanish bar and restaurant.
Boulevardier is a speakeasy-style whiskey bar.
The hotel offers complimentary premium Wi-Fi.
In-room dining is available from 6:00 am to 10:00 pm.
The design is a careful restoration of the original 1946 building.

highlights.text: The Colonial One-Bedroom Suite has a wood-burning fireplace.
The Penthouse Suite is on the fifth floor.
The restoration includes architectural treasures salvaged from demolished colonial convents.

considerations.text: The airport is 40 minutes from the hotel by car.
Spa treatments run from 10:00 am to 7:00 pm.
The colonial quarter is 20 minutes from the hotel by car.
WhataHotel notes that the smaller property size limits facilities compared to larger resorts.

perks.text: With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, breakfast for two is free daily.
With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, guests get a priority upgrade if available at check-in.
With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, guests get a $100 hotel credit.
WhataHotel special offers can be combined with the exclusive perks.
With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, guests get free Wi-Fi access.
